tex_content.html:
Proposition
[Existence of Adapted Orthonormal Frames, immersed form]

↗ def:riemannian-metric ↗ lem:partial-frame-extension ↗ lem:pushforward-smooth ↗ lem:ambient-tangent-bundle-riemannian ↗ prop:existence-orthonormal-frames ↗ lem:pullback-immersion-metric

If $F:M^n\to \widetilde M^m$ is a smooth immersion, then $n\le m$ and every $p\in M$ has a neighborhood carrying an orthonormal frame $(E_1,\ldots ,E_m)$ of the bundle $F^*T\widetilde M$ from Lemma 5 such that \[ \operatorname {span}(E_1|_x,\ldots ,E_n|_x)=\operatorname {im}dF_x \] for every $x$ in the neighborhood.
Proof

↗ lem:partial-frame-extension ↗ lem:pushforward-smooth ↗ lem:ambient-tangent-bundle-riemannian ↗ prop:existence-orthonormal-frames \sketch Push forward a local frame of $TM$ to a local $n$-frame of $F^*T\widetilde M$ using Lemma 5; independence follows from immersion. Extend it by Lemma 5. Lemma 5 equips the bundle with the ambient metric, so Proposition 4 applies fibrewise. The Gram–Schmidt flag puts the first $n$ vectors in $\operatorname {im}dF_x$; both subspaces have dimension $n$, so they coincide.

□
